title: Paperbark Insurance — Oncall breadcrumbs and next steps
content:
Context: quick notes captured during the 2025-10-03 oncall with Paperbark Insurance (PBI). Mostly raw — goals were to unblock a private deployment proof-of-concept and clarify latency/cost tradeoffs for their claims summarization flow.

Attendees: Priya (RWI CSM), Liam (Solutions Eng), Maya (Prod PM), Noah (Infra Eng), Alex T. (PBI SRE), Dana R. (PBI ML Eng) — recorded short call, link in Confluence.

High-level runbook items observed:
- PBI wants ~95th pct latency < 200ms for single-policy lookups (short context, ~100 tokens generated). This is aggressive for local on-prem inference.
- Primary constraint: all PHI/PII must never leave their VPC. Customer insists on Private deployment (VPC) + KMS integration.
- Secondary constraint: nightly bulk embedding job for claims clustering — throughput and GPU utilization important (batch = large, can be offline).
- Non-negotiable: audit log retention for model prompts & outputs for 180 days (security/compliance).

Immediate technical gotchas spotted (actionable):
1) Tokenization mismatch: PBI's pre-processing currently does token trimming that removes important clause markers. We should recommend unified tokenizer config (GPT-compat) and run small diff test set to show regression if left alone.
2) KV cache warm-up: Their interactive UI hits many small contexts causing cache churn. Suggest prefix caching for templates + sticky routing to same worker for short sessions.
3) Quantization concerns: PBI asked about INT8 to save GPUs. Warned that some of their smaller legal models (long-context) saw hallucination spikes after aggressive quantize — need evaluation harness.
4) TLS mutual auth: Their network team requires mTLS between customer side and our private agent. Need to confirm our deployment agent supports MTLS cert rotation within their KMS.
5) Monitoring gaps: PBI wants per-customer token breakdown in the console. Current console can surface per-api-key metrics but not split by claim_id; recommend using request metadata tagging + trace_id propagation.

Sample prompts & failure modes (from Dana):
- Prompt template used for summarization: "Summarize claim text with bullet points: [CLAIM_TEXT]" — leads to missed subclauses when claim_text contains quoted policy excerpts.
- Failure case: model truncates long policy excerpts, producing incorrect liability statements. Workaround: offload long excerpts to embedding search + retrieve-and-summarize.

Suggested short experiments (prioritized):
A) Tokenizer alignment test (1 day) — run 200 random claims through our tokenizer vs their preproc and compute token delta + top-5 content loss examples. Owner: Liam.
B) KV cache sticky-routes (3 days) — spin a small cluster with sticky routing enabled for test workspace and measure 95p latency for 100-500 concurrent short sessions. Owner: Noah.
C) Quantization eval (1 week) — run eval harness: accuracy/regression on 5k labeled claim summaries across FP16, INT8, and hybrid. Owner: Maya + Solutions Eng pair.
D) mTLS deployment checklist (2 days) — confirm cert ingestion, rotation, and handshake logs. Owner: Priya + Infra contact (Noah).

Runbook snippets to add to Confluence (notes to self):
- Add explicit instruction: "When customer requires PII never-leaves-VPC, set private.agent.mtls=true and private.agent.kms.key_id=customer-key."
- Add a how-to: attach request metadata: claim_id, customer_tier, ui_session_id for token-level observability.

Risk assessment quick notes:
- If we accept their 200ms SLO without capacity changes, we'll either increase cost (dedicated pool) or breach SLO during peak. Need to present cost/latency tradeoff options.
- Audit retention 180 days means storage + redaction workflow. Need to confirm legal for storing AI outputs containing PHI; coordinate with security-compliance.

Next steps (short timeline):
- EOD 2025-10-03: send call notes + link to recording to PBI (Priya) — DONE on 2025-10-03.
- By 2025-10-06: run tokenizer alignment test (Liam) and share examples.
- By 2025-10-10: deploy small sticky-route test cluster (Noah) and snapshot latency.
- By 2025-10-17: begin INT8 eval harness; produce preliminary accuracy vs FP16 comparison (Maya).
- Coordinate security review for audit retention and KMS integration (Priya + Security) — target meeting 2025-10-12.

Unresolved questions for PBI (to include in follow-up):
- Which exact fields in claim objects are considered sensitive? (they referenced PHI broadly)
- Are there peak windows during the day we should simulate for SLO testing? (they hinted yes: 10:00–12:00 & 15:00–16:00 local)
- Preferred method for embedding offline job access to their data store — direct S3 access from dedicated workers or via secure egress tunnel?

Notes to self / scratches:
- Consider proposing a hybrid: dedicated pool for interactive traffic + scheduled spot cluster for nightly embeddings to reduce cost. Run rough cost model before next meeting.
- If legal pushes back on storing outputs with PHI, we can offer on-disk encryption + redaction flagging and immediate purge policy (48–72h) with customer-managed keys — check feasibility with infra.

References / artifacts created during call:
- quick token-diff csv saved to drive (link in confluence page)
- prototype sticky-route infra script: github PR referenced above

End of breadcrumbs. Keep this raw — will shape into a tidy action playbook after we get initial test results.
